situation:
You are the promotions manager at NORTHWIRE ESPORTS GROUP, a company that owns a professional esports team and operates a regional amateur league. The vice president of marketing (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should promote the one program it will run in its arena this off-season, and which audience that promotion should be aimed at.

NORTHWIRE completed its merger with CROWNPOST GAMING LEAGUE eight months ago and has not finished combining the two organizations. The arena, the event staff and the mobile ticketing app came from NORTHWIRE; the amateur league's teenage members and their family mailing list came from CROWNPOST. The two fan lists still sit in separate systems, and nobody has settled which audience the combined company sells to its sponsors.

The arena stage can support one program during the eight open weeks between seasons, not both. A summer training camp for the league's teenage members would fill every one of those weeks, but its advertising would have to speak to parents, and camp fees earn far less per week than ticketed events do.

Creator weekends built around streaming personalities would reach the eighteen-to-twenty-four fans sponsors pay to reach, but they would close the arena floor to the league families who were promised summer access when the merger was announced. The vice president of marketing (judge) wants you to identify the market the off-season program should serve, coordinate the promotional activities that would reach it, and explain what each advertisement would need to contain.

You should also explain how you would bring the ticketing and league staff from both former companies behind whichever program you choose, and how the mobile ticketing app should be used to sell it. The vice president of marketing (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of marketing (judge) at NORTHWIRE ESPORTS GROUP. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are responsible for what the merged company puts its name behind, and the off-season is the first calendar the two former organizations have had to plan together. You want to hear which market the promotions manager would aim the off-season program at, how the promotional activities would be coordinated, what the advertisements would carry, and how the staff of both former companies would be brought behind the choice.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: What would tell us next spring that we picked the right program?
If we chose the wrong audience, how would we find that out?
